name: Phenibut
toxicity: potentially lethal when mixed with depressants like alcohol, benzodiazepines or opioids
summary: A derivative of GABA with the addition of a phenyl ring which allows it to cross the blood brain barrier. The drug is typically used as an anxiety and insomnia medication. Tolerance and physical dependency builds quickly.
advisory: Avoid: CNS depressants such as alcohol, opioids, and benzodiazepines.
doseBasis: NOTE: The substance reportedly has a very fast increase in tolerance which seems to vary significantly person-to-person. Caution is recommended start slowly and increase dosages incrementally. There are suggestions to start with lower dosages (50-100mg's) and to wait two weeks before dosage increasement.

tolerance.buildUp: within a couple of days of continuous use

pharmacology.text: Phenibut acts as a full agonist of the GABAB receptor, similarly to baclofen. It has between 30- and 68-fold lower affinity for the GABAB receptor than baclofen, and, in accordance, is used at far higher doses in comparison. (R)-Phenibut has more than 100-fold higher affinity for the GABAB receptor than does (S)-phenibut; hence, (R)-phenibut is the active enantiomer at the GABAB receptor.

uses.text: Phenibut, sold under the brand name Anvifen among others, is a central nervous system (CNS) depressant with anxiolytic effects, and is used to treat anxiety, insomnia, and for a variety of other indications. It is usually taken orally (swallowed by mouth), but may be given intravenously. The medication is structurally related to the neurotransmitter γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA), and hence is a GABA analogue.
uses.recreational: Phenibut is used recreationally due to its ability to produce euphoria, anxiolysis, and increased sociability, as well as remaining undetected in routine urinalysis.

sideEffects.text: Side effects of phenibut can include sedation, sleepiness, nausea, irritability, agitation, dizziness, euphoria, and sometimes headache, among others.
